narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 52% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability tipped above 50%, the admissions system automatically rejected your law school application.

Your rejection was driven primarily by three pieces of information, ranked by importance. First, your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest factor. You placed in the second decile, far below the average of roughly sixth decile among students who were accepted. This low ranking strongly pushed the model toward expecting you to struggle with the bar exam.

Second, your family income bracket worked in the opposite direction. Being in the middle-income group slightly improved the prediction because most accepted students also come from similar or higher brackets. However, this positive influence was not large enough to offset the other factors.

Third, your undergraduate GPA of 2.5, compared with an average of 3.23 among accepted students, also nudged the prediction slightly toward failure, though its effect was smaller than your class rank.

Taken together, your relatively low academic performance in law school and college outweighed the modest benefit from your family background, leading the model to forecast that you are slightly more likely than not to fail the bar on the first try.

You should focus on strengthening your academic record, consider retaking key courses, or explore bar-preparation programs that have helped students with similar profiles succeed. Improving those academic signals will be the most direct way to change future predictions in your favor. (248 words)

Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the law school application was denied for this student.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on students who took the bar exam.

The target variable is whether the student passed the bar exam on the first try (0 = passed, 1 = failed).

Protected attributes gender and race were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward "will fail" (bar exam failure), negative toward "will pass" (bar exam success). Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. STUDENT PROFILE 
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific person who is rejected law school admission.

Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
